Namespace ParquetNeo.ColumnTypes

Classes

ColumnSettings

What can be adjusted about the column a type is written to. A type takes the settings that suit it (see SupportedSettings) and ignores the others.

ColumnType

What every column type says without knowing its .NET type: which one it is, the column it creates, and whether a column fits it. Derive from ColumnType<TValue>, which adds reading and writing, to add a type of your own.

ColumnTypeRegistry

Finds the ColumnType<TValue> that reads and writes values of a .NET type: the built-in ones, any enum (as the name of its value), and the ones added with Register<TValue>(ColumnType<TValue>). The serializer uses it to decide how a property is stored, so registering a column type teaches it a new type for its properties.

ColumnType<TValue>

Everything about storing one .NET type in a Parquet column: the column it gets by default, which columns of a file it can be read from or written to, and how a batch of values is converted to and from the physical type and passed to the column reader or writer. The built-in types are found with ColumnTypeRegistry; an own type derives from this class.
